claims.text: Exposure to direct-acting antivirals is associated with a decrease in all-cause mortality in adult patients with chronic hepatitis C virus infection after adjusting for confounding variables.

Exposure to direct-acting antivirals is associated with a decrease in hepatocellular carcinoma incidence in adult patients with chronic hepatitis C virus infection after adjusting for confounding variables.
Exposure to direct-acting antivirals is not associated with decompensated cirrhosis in adult patients with chronic hepatitis C virus infection after adjusting for confounding variables.

evidence.description: After adjustment for variables, exposure to direct-acting antivirals was associated with a decrease in all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.33-0.70).
After adjustment for variables, exposure to direct-acting antivirals was associated with a decrease in hepatocellular carcinoma (adjusted HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.46-0.93).
After adjustment for variables, exposure to direct-acting antivirals was not associated with decompensated cirrhosis (adjusted HR 1.14, 95% CI 0.57-2.27).

methodologies.name: Time-dependent Cox proportional hazards modeling in prospective cohort
methodologies.description: Quantified the association between direct-acting antiviral treatment and clinical outcomes (all-cause mortality, hepatocellular carcinoma, decompensated cirrhosis) using multivariable time-dependent Cox proportional hazards models.
conditions: Adult patients with chronic HCV infection
Excluded history of decompensated cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, or liver transplantation
Excluded prior interferon-ribavirin treatment with or without first-generation protease inhibitors
